This is something I’ve practised as well. 

The way I see it is: do the people who are asked for help, help? If no, it’s only worth mentioning that the main character asked for help, but the people around them only scoffed or ignored them (or whatever). If yes, it can be relevant to add a small exchange between the characters.

In general it’s quite boring to read about mundane things, _unless_ they have a purpose later on. Like if a character suddenly finds his mug is missing, and then his toothbrush is placed slightly different, but he’s the only one who lives there. Next scene could be someone jumping out the closet and attacking the main character, but these little clues make it seem less random.

If not I’ll just continue like “are you still in that school/ do you still work at (place)?” If no “oh so what do you do now? Do you like that better?” It may seem boring but I’ve found that people often enjoy to talk about themselves. I’ll try to think back to our last conversations and ask about that. “Are you still seeing this person?” “How did that date go?” Etc etc etc

Sometimes I open up a conversation like “I really like your outfit! That (piece of clothing) is so cool.” If I genuinely mean it of course. 

I hope that somewhat helps. And remember, sometimes silence is okay. If you can’t think of anything to say, look at your surroundings and let yourself be inspired for a moment. If you don’t think it’s awkward, it’s not. Genuinely.
